text.en: A tree of connections shows how people, animals, plants and ideas travel and grow together on one Earth.

These stories are of people, journeys, sharing and the blending of cultures. We speak different languages and play different games, but we learn from and inspire one another.
Interview a grandparent or neighbour about a food, song or custom that was not there in their childhood but is common now, and find where it came from.
List the things that came to India from other countries and those that travelled from India, and trace them on a map with two coloured strings.
There is an ancient Indian saying: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, which means the world is one family.
Our Earth is more than land and water. It is a living web of life where people, animals, plants and ideas travel, mix and grow together.
All people, animals, trees, rivers and even the air and sky belong to this family. We depend on each other and share the same home.
When we see the world as one family we live with respect, care and love for one another and for the Earth that supports us.
Angkor Wat in Cambodia is the largest temple in the world.
Earth needs care too. When we care for the Earth we care for each other, because we are one family. Earth is a gift we must protect for ourselves, for others and for the future.
The logo of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change shows the balance between nature and human life, and reminds us that caring for the environment means caring for ourselves.
Let us reflect: write what Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam teaches in your own words, how we can live like one big family even when we are different, and one way you can care for the Earth.
(additional, not in the textbook) We can care for the Earth by saving water and energy, avoiding waste and planting trees.
The logo of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change shows the balance between nature and human life. It reminds us that humans and nature are connected and must live in harmony, and caring for the environment means caring for ourselves too.
Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam teaches that the whole world is one family. We can live like one big family even when we are different, by respecting, sharing and caring for each other.
Reflect: pick one idea and write a short story of how it travelled from one place to another long ago. Write one way you can care for the Earth. Think of an item that can travel from India to other parts of the world.
Seasons' Journal: at the end of the book there is a journal to make four entries in the year, once every term, observing the same place. Record five themes: plant life, birds and animals, air, heat and light, water and water bodies, and human activities.
Simple notes, drawings or something you found can be pasted. The terms are April-June, July-September, October-December and January-March.

prompt.en: How can we show that Earth is our shared home?

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking only our own place matters

points.en: Earth is a living web of life.
We care through learning, sharing and respect.
